stocks.name: Ameriprise Financial
stocks.thesis: Recurring advice fees and high operating leverage support compounding; the price leaves room for moderate growth. Normalize market-sensitive earnings rather than extrapolating record markets.
stocks.countercase: Equity markets, client cash yields and fund outflows can weaken together; regulated capital is not spare cash.
stocks.failure_rule: Two quarters of wealth net outflows, normalized annual earning power below $40, or an unexplained regulatory-capital deterioration: suspend additions and revalue.

baseline.notes: Q1 adjusted earnings benefit is $25m, distinct from $28m gross revenue in 10-Q. Rounded down. No separate capital addition.

stocks.terminal_period: FY2029-equivalent annual earning power; three growth steps from normalized FY2026
stocks.condition: Price alone is insufficient: recheck thesis, event risk and portfolio capacity.
stocks.slot_note: Funded slot in the model portfolio

stocks.name: Paychex
stocks.thesis: Payroll and compliance workflows are sticky. Modest growth, integration improvements and dividends can justify the entry without a return to historic premium valuations.
stocks.countercase: Paycor integration, borrowing and cash-conversion weakness can erode the apparent yield advantage.
stocks.failure_rule: Normalized FY2027 EPS below $5.50, persistent owner cash below $1.7bn without documented reversible timing, or debt-funded dividends: suspend additions and revalue.
stocks.baseline: Management FY2026 adjusted EPS5.51 multiplied by midpoint FY2027 guidance growth8%; company-adjusted, not GAAP. Our FY2027 economic anchor5.85 retains0.10/share recurring integration allowance.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.thesis: Azure, Microsoft 365 and enterprise distribution support durable earnings; remove investment gains and retain stock compensation.
stocks.countercase: Heavy AI spending, finance leases and competition can weaken cash returns despite strong accounting earnings.
stocks.failure_rule: Two quarters of weakening cloud growth with continued capital-intensity increases, or a material cut to operating-margin earning power: rebuild the valuation.
stocks.terminal_period: FY2029 ending June 2029; completed fiscal year at September 2029 exit
stocks.condition: Price alone is insufficient: recheck thesis, event risk and portfolio capacity.
stocks.slot_note: Funded slot in the model portfolio

stocks.name: NVIDIA
stocks.thesis: Accelerated computing demand and platform economics support growth, but the base case already requires a very large revenue expansion.
stocks.countercase: Customer concentration, export restrictions and extraordinary supply, cloud and investment commitments make the downside highly nonlinear.
stocks.failure_rule: Material customer financing stress, cancelled demand, sustained gross margin below 65%, or commitments rising while orders slow: suspend additions and rebuild bear/base cases.
stocks.terminal_period: FY2030 ending January 2030; four months forward at September 2029 exit
stocks.condition: Price alone is insufficient: recheck thesis, event risk and portfolio capacity.

stocks.name: Allegion

stocks.countercase: Acquisitions, international disruption and construction weakness can impair margins and cash conversion.
stocks.failure_rule: Two quarters of negative Americas organic growth with over 200bp margin deterioration, or weak cash conversion without a documented bridge: cancel entry and revalue.

stocks.name: The Hartford
stocks.thesis: Core underwriting and disciplined insurance pricing can compound book value. Strip favorable prior-year reserve development and normalize partnership income.
stocks.countercase: Catastrophes, reserve deficiencies, social inflation and credit losses can arrive together.
stocks.failure_rule: Underlying accident-year underwriting deteriorates persistently, adverse development reverses the reserve thesis, or capital weakens: stop additions and review reduction.

baseline.notes: Remove all favorable Q2 PYD and LP yield above 5%; retain actual Q2 CAT charge. Do not add Q1 core EPS without removing discontinued Hartford Funds. Annualizing a quarter is a starting point, not annual guidance.

stocks.name: Corpay
stocks.thesis: Corporate payments can support high-single-digit earnings growth; explicitly charge stock compensation and recurring integration costs.
stocks.countercase: Leverage, regulatory expenses and recurring acquisition costs can consume cash. Client funds are not distributable corporate cash.
stocks.failure_rule: Two quarters of organic growth below 5%, leverage above 3.5x with weak debt repayment, or a material customer-funds/compliance failure: cancel entry and revalue.

stocks.name: Assurant
stocks.thesis: Connected-living services and housing insurance have useful recurring economics; valuation must include a normal catastrophe allowance.
stocks.countercase: A benign catastrophe year and reserve releases can flatter run-rate earnings. Distribution concentration and claims inflation remain important.
stocks.failure_rule: Repeated catastrophe/claims experience above the normalized allowance or weakening program economics: increase the loss allowance and reduce the entry value.

limitations: Analyst scenarios, not calibrated forecasts or probabilities.
The new portfolio has no validated historical track record.
Bear terminal values are not maximum drawdowns.
Tax residency, US-person status, holdings, access, commissions and liabilities are unknown. Model is new-money USD capital with no leverage.
Conditional stock slots are not simultaneous instructions; cash stays in reserve until limits and thesis tests both pass.
ETF expense ratios are fund expenses; scenarios are after assumed fund expenses, before personal tax and trading costs.
